The sky is blue because of the way light travels through the air. Sunlight is white, but it is made up of many different colors, each with a different wavelength. When sunlight passes through the atmosphere, the shorter wavelengths (blue and violet) are scattered more than the longer ones (red, orange, yellow). This scattering is called Rayleigh scattering.

Blue light is scattered in all directions by the gases and particles in the air, which makes the sky appear blue to us. Even though violet light is scattered more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue, and the sun emits more blue light than violet, so we see the sky as blue.

At sunrise or sunset, the sky turns red or orange because the light has to pass through more air, and the blue light is scattered away, leaving the longer wavelengths to dominate.
